So I built a messaging service where you stay anonymous, until enough people like you

I posted this in your other deleted thread, but:

I love the idea. It's unique. Celebrities won't get attention simply for being celebrities, and hidden genius can be discovered.

Edit: I think it needs a FAQ on the site. What is the threshold for losing anonymity? I suppose it matters depending on how explosive a comment is. Millions of likes probably won't happen unless the site is getting that kind of traffic, so initially, everyone will be anonymous. Is that accurate?

Thanks for the great feedback!

Currently the threshold for losing anonymity is low. However, this will go up as usage and overall likes increase. You're right...a FAQ needs to go up soon.

Between Twitter and Whisper, I felt there was a third way. A microblogging service that is anonymous only some of the time.

I named it SaidWho.

How does it work? Every post is anonymous in the beginning.

But if it gets enough likes, you can see who wrote it. Nobody knows who you are, until enough people actually like you.

Edit: the more you are revealed, the higher your Reveal Score is. You can see this score on your profile page.
I'm probably missing something basic here but what if you want to stay anonymous?
Theres nothing to force anonymity on a post forever- yet. The idea is that if you're loved, you've got every reason to show yourself.

The idea isn't built around anonymity, but around recognizing good content based on the content itself, and not based on who posted it.

It's to prevent things getting exposure just because someone famous said it. Every post will have to stand on it's own merit.
